newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks mixed, short-term growth possible.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks mixed, short-term growth possible.

text.p: Croatian stocks were mixed on Tuesday with leading issues forging ahead and traders predicted short-term recovery was possible in the days ahead.
"It's about time that trade picked up again. The prices are approaching the bottom limit they last hit in December," said Velimir Zelimorski of FIMA brokerage.
Another trader, Marko Delic of the Raiffeisen Bank, foresaw "a small short-term boom", followed by stagnation.
"Some investors may have returned, but most activity is speculation," he said.
Eight of 17 active stocks rose on Tuesday, seven fell and two were flat. Volume was slightly higher at 11,487 shares and turnover shrank to seven million kuna.
Market heavyweights drugs firm Pliva and Zagrebacka Banka, both of which trade their Global Depositary Receipts (GDRs) in London, rose.
Pliva added 20 kuna or 4.5 percent to 460. With 3,463 shares sold it was the day's most active stock.
Zagrebacka's ordinary shares climbed 40 kuna to 2,140 on volume of 1,583 units. Its preference E-series, highly rated by traders, gained 39 kuna to 1,199, selling 150 shares.
The biggest gainer was insurer Croatia Osiguranje's A-series, which added 300 kuna or 31.5 percent to 1,250 from last October, but sold only 20 shares.

The firm, Croatia's largest insurer, said on Tuesday it had reversed a five-year negative trend, recorded a 2.2 pct growth in premium income and 7.3 percent in profit in 1996 and paid 69 percent higher dividend than last year.
Varazdinska Banka, which lost 15 kuna or six percent to 235 was the biggest decliner. It sold 400 shares,
Traders put the bank's decline down to swollen supply of shares, following a recent share split. But Zelimorski said the stock was currently undervalued, given the quality of the firm.
Food processor Podravka and chocolate maker Kras, both expected to follow in the footsteps of the leading issues, sold relatively large volumes.
Podravka inched up two kuna to 262 on volume of 2,272 shares, while Kras held its ground at 410 kuna with 1,126 units sold.

Delic said Podravka was not likely to rise above 270 kuna, as there were many selling offers in the range between 265-275 kuna. The firm has yet to publish its annual results, which are rumoured to be negative.
